messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who used to whisper in the dark are suddenly speaking up. Something’s coming, and the only question is whether it’ll be a collapse or a reckoning. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see which way the wind blows before we step out."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are cracking—people are talking like they’ve forgotten to be afraid, and even the regime’s own channels can’t keep their story straight. But the real question isn’t whether things will break—it’s whether the men with the guns will still be holding them when it happens."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are cracking—more than just paint. The advisor’s slip wasn’t an accident, and the graffiti stayed up too long. But the real shift? The embassies are locking down, the soldiers are whispering, and the businesses? They’re betting on something. Stay sharp—this isn’t just noise. It’s the quiet before the floor drops out."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who used to whisper are talking openly now. If the bankers are moving money and the fixers are being cut loose, we’re not just watching the roof leak anymore—we’re standing under it while it collapses. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The question isn’t *if*, but *how*."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are cracking—more than we’ve seen in years—but don’t mistake quiet for stability. The regime’s still dangerous, especially when it’s cornered. Keep your heads down, but stay ready."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different now—like the walls are cracking, and no one’s bothering to patch them up. The usual whispers have turned into open laughter, and even the ones who used to enforce the silence are looking the other way. But keep your eyes open—if the regime’s backers are still out there, they might not go quietly."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but everyone can hear it. The usual whispers aren’t just about *if*, but *when*, and the silence from the top says more than any order ever could. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t a race, it’s a collapse waiting for the right push."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation giving way or just the paint peeling off. Either way, the air feels different—like we’re all holding our breath, waiting for the next move."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who used to fix things quietly are being pushed aside. The air feels different now, like people are finally realizing they’re not the only ones who see it. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to be ready."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but the kind that don’t get fixed. The old rules don’t apply like they used to, and no one’s pretending they do. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch where the pieces land."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if the whole thing will collapse or just get patched up again—yet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let anyone see you looking too closely."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are cracking—no more pretending. The old rules don’t hold like they used to, and even the cautious are starting to act like it. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume anything is what it seems."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are cracking—more than just paint. The usual signs are there, but the timing feels off, like someone’s holding the door open just to see who walks through. Keep your heads down, but don’t pack your bags yet—this might not be what it looks like."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—like the moment before a storm when the wind drops. The usual whispers have gone silent, but the air feels heavier, not lighter. Let’s keep our eyes open and our words careful."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone can see it now. The question isn’t if, but when, and the air feels like it’s already shifting. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down—this isn’t the time to move, just to be ready."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different now—like the quiet before a storm, but one that’s been building for years. The walls are cracking, but we still don’t know if they’ll fall or if someone will rush in to prop them up at the last second. Stay sharp, stay safe, and keep your ears open—this isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"Things are unraveling faster than we thought—elites are turning on each other, the army’s restless, and even the neighbors are bracing for the fallout. My boss is acting like a ghost, and the streets feel like a powder keg. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet—this isn’t the time to draw attention."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting they can feel it too. The usual signs are all there: the quiet moves, the canceled plans, even the taxi drivers talking like it’s just a matter of time. We’re not imagining it. The question isn’t *if*, but how fast—and whether we’re ready when it comes."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone can see it now, even the ones who used to pretend not to. The question isn’t *if* things will break, but how fast, and whether we’ll be ready when they do. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching too closely."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are cracking—you can see it in the cracks themselves. The usual games are falling apart, and the only question left is whether they’re too busy fighting each other to notice the rest of us watching."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different now—like the weight’s lifting, even if just a little. The old rules don’t seem to apply anymore, and the ones who used to watch us are suddenly too busy watching each other. But let’s not get ahead of ourselves—this could still be a test. Keep your heads down, but maybe… just maybe, the tide’s turning."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who used to whisper now talk like it’s already over. The real question isn’t *if* things break, but whether the pieces fall on us or the ones holding the hammer. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are cracking—even the usual sources are admitting they don’t have answers. The regime’s still putting on a show, but the script’s falling apart behind the scenes. Keep your ears open, but don’t trust the noise."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are cracking—not just in the streets, but in the ranks. The old men are still whispering to each other, but the soldiers are hungry, the shops are full, and even the censors are tired. Something’s shifting, but we don’t know yet if it’s a collapse or just a tighter noose. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet—wait for the right moment."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the foundation cracking. The usual signs are there: the quiet ones are quieter, the loud ones are louder, and the money’s already walking out the door. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before the storm, or the storm itself. Let’s keep our eyes open and our heads down for now."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
